correctness.rationale: The classical Eulerian exact formula reduces E_n to G(n) modulo 2^k after n>=max(4,k); the even chart U has odd divided difference, so exact 2-adic isometry. The four odd charts W_r have sharp difference valuation 4+v2(h), from the explicit q=6561 subtraction with mod-four quotient 2; two charts lie in each of 0 and 10 mod16. Fiber counts are 9 or 1; small powers follow by reduction. The even chart and parity obstruction prove least eventual period 2^{k+1}. The extracted independent checker passed 101 recurrence, 24570 fiber, 49140 period and 3810 isometry comparisons. Finite tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Multiple published-finding corpus searches for fixed three-descent Eulerian all-level dyadic residue counts and relevant mathematical literature show no identified covering statement. Full primary published results for the two-descent Eulerian column (two uniform fibers) and for cubic binomial column (five-to-one fibers) have different objects and imply neither the present nine-to-one distribution nor its odd-chart proof. Cao–Pan concerns Eulerian sums across columns, and Krattenthaler–Müller central Eulerian congruences; their relevant primary accessible texts do not state this result. OEIS A000498 supplies the classical exact formula without an evaluated all-modulus fiber theorem in the inspected excerpt. Castro et al. 2015 full text inaccessible: explicit priority risk, and search absence cannot prove unique priority.
residual_risks: The 2015 Castro–González–Medina full text could not be inspected; an implicit stronger fixed-column valuation/residue theorem may be present.
OEIS A000498 complete entry could not be inspected due to HTTP 403; only indexed excerpt was available.
Unindexed preprints, appendices and equivalent higher-column general theorems might predate this claim. A negative search does not prove novelty.

value.rationale: The 3-descent Eulerian column is a standard natural combinatorial sequence whose exact dyadic value distribution is not determined by its known formula or by fixed-row congruences. This theorem completely classifies infinite-level value multiplicities, least eventual periods and Haar density, and gives a structurally motivated contrast to the uniformly distributed 2-descent column. Two explicit 2-adic target balls have ninefold rather than singleton multiplicity, explained by four 2-adic charts; this is more than a routine finite test or generic formula substitution.
